settings.name: columns
settings.doc: Columns, or groups of them (a group's header needs the spans feature; the base keeps its columns).

settings.name: messages
settings.doc: Required (D1): the grid bundles no language.

settings.name: direction
settings.doc: `auto` follows the host's direction, and its changes.

settings.name: headers
settings.doc: `'hidden'`: no header row on screen, kept for screen readers and shown while the keyboard is in it (docs/behaviors/hidden-headers.md, 1.9.0). Live. Default `'shown'`.

settings.name: multiSort
settings.doc: False: one sort only — Shift+click, Shift+Enter and a header part's `toggleSort(true)` act as a plain click (sort.md « One sort only »); the app's own `sort.set` of several is kept. True by default. Fixed.

settings.name: sameRow
settings.doc: A full reload (`rows` again, a server's answer) compares a row kept by id with its new copy: equal, it is unchanged and keeps its old object, so only real changes flash (row-identity-transactions.md « Rows compared by value »; `sameValues` from `@dzgrid/core/compare`). A throw: changed, one warning per load. Fixed.

settings.name: rowHeight
settings.doc: The row height in px at 16 px text, over the density's (owner D1, virtual-scroll.md « Row height »): from 24 to 1 000, grown with the reader's text size; header rows follow unless `headerHeight` is set. Anything else is told (`invalid-setting`, a warning) and the density's height is used. Live.

settings.name: headerHeight
settings.doc: The column headers' row and the column-group rows above it, in px at 16 px text (density.md « Header height », 1.9.0): the same rule as `rowHeight` (24 to 1 000, grown with the text size, else told and ignored); a feature's row under the headers (the filter row) keeps the row height. Absent: the row height. Live. 1.10.0: `{ columns, groups }` sets them apart (« Group rows' height »): `columns` absent the row height, `groups` absent the columns'.

settings.name: selection
settings.type: { readonly mode: 'none' | 'single' | 'multi'; readonly checkbox?: boolean; readonly click?: boolean; readonly keepOnFilter?: boolean; readonly canSelect?: (row: DataNode<T>, selection: SelectionState, context: unknown) => boolean | string }
settings.doc: `keepOnFilter`: false clears the selection when a filter or the search changes (a sort or a page never does); true by default, rows ticked stay ticked even once hidden. `canSelect` (step 21, docs/behaviors/selection-rules.md, needs `rules()`): whether a row may join the selection; true allows, false refuses, a string refuses and is said ('' refuses unsaid). Never asked to untick; its `selection` keeps changing while one action is vetted (copy it to keep it).

settings.name: context
settings.doc: The application's own context (step 21): handed to every part (`context`), `canSelect`, the export's `canExport` and the tooltip callback. Live; a new value is a new identity (pass a new object).

settings.name: rowClass
settings.doc: Classes for a data row from its data (showcase themes step 6, cell-class.md): space-separated, null for none; asked when the row is bound again (another row, new data, columns, language, context or rule). Live. Keep the same function from one update to the next: a new one (an inline arrow) binds every row again.

settings.name: busy
settings.doc: The host is reloading rows it keeps on screen (a poll, its own arrows; 1.4.0, overlays.md « Busy bar »): `aria-busy` on the grid at once, a thin bar under the header after 200 ms (held 400 ms once shown), never with the loading overlay. A server's request with rows kept shows it by itself. Live; nothing announced.

settings.name: label
settings.doc: The grid's accessible name, already translated; the bundle's `grid.label` otherwise.

settings.name: injectStyles
settings.doc: False when the host loads the layout CSS itself (strict CSP).

settings.name: overscan
settings.type: { readonly rows?: number; readonly cols?: number }

settings.name: searchWarmup
settings.doc: `idle` prepares the quick search after each load, in idle time, so the first keystroke is instant — at the cost of holding the search caches (627 bytes a row measured on dataset A's ten text columns; budget for the owner, D13). Off by default (D13).

settings.name: parts
settings.doc: Parts by name: a column says `ui: { cell: 'statusBadge' }`, or a part replaces a default for a type (`'cell.number'`). One registry per grid.

settings.name: source
settings.doc: A server's rows: `sourceRows(data, …)` from `@dzgrid/core/server`. Live: another source asks again.

settings.name: operations
settings.doc: Where filter, search, sort and page run (`'server'`, `'client'`, or per operation). Set once.

settings.name: pagination
settings.doc: Paged in the browser: one page of the filtered, sorted rows at a time. Set once.

settings.name: filterKinds
settings.doc: Custom filter kinds (docs/behaviors/filter-custom.md), for the browser's filter and a server's. Set once.

settings.name: clock
settings.doc: The clock (milliseconds since 1970 UTC) date shortcuts count from (filter-relative.md); `Date.now` by default. Set once.

settings.name: fullWidth
settings.doc: Rows drawn as one cell across the whole width (a title, a note): true, or the part that draws it. Needs the spans feature; the base ignores it.

settings.name: motion
settings.doc: False: no motion (`@dzgrid/dom/motion-gsap` stops, `data-motion="off"` on the root for the theme). Live.

settings.name: theme
settings.doc: CSS variables written on the grid's root, by typed keys (`{ rowOddBg: '…', headerWeight: 500 }`; presentation-settings.md 20–22, 1.9.0). Needs `theming()` from `@dzgrid/dom/theme`; a bad key or value is told (`invalid-setting`) and skipped. Live.

settings.name: icons
settings.doc: The application's own icons for the grid's marks (presentation-settings.md 17–19). Needs `theming()`. Live.

settings.name: features
settings.doc: Optional features (`filters()`, `pagination()`…), set up once with the grid.

columns.name: id
columns.doc: Required and stable: the key of the column's state.

columns.name: field
columns.doc: A path into the row (`a.b.c`); defaults to the id when no `value` is given.

columns.name: header
columns.doc: Already translated by the host.

columns.name: headerShort
columns.doc: A shorter header, without unit, where room is short (the pivot's created headers and chips, pivot.md 38); absent: `header`.

columns.name: hideable
columns.doc: `false`: the column menu's « Hide » is disabled for it (Phase 6 step 3, column-menu.md 13).

columns.name: menu
columns.doc: `false`: no column menu (no ⋮, no right-click menu; its keys left to the page). Phase 6 step 3.

columns.name: chooser
columns.doc: `false`: left out of the column chooser's list (still hideable by the menu). Phase 6 step 4, columns-chooser.md 6.

columns.name: groupable
columns.doc: `false`: rows are never grouped by it (`@dzgrid/core/grouping`, row-grouping.md 14; the zone and the menu refuse it). Phase 7.

columns.name: aggFunc
columns.doc: Its total on group rows, footers and the grand total (`@dzgrid/core/grouping`, aggregation.md 2–3): a built-in, or a function of the group's values. The grouping's own `aggFuncs` win over it. Phase 7.

columns.name: total
columns.doc: Its total in the totals row of a flat grid (`@dzgrid/dom/totals-row`, docs/behaviors/totals-row.md; 1.9.0): the same built-ins and rules as `aggFunc`, or a function of the column's values (`level` null). Needs that feature.

columns.name: headerVertical
columns.doc: Its header's title written upwards (`@dzgrid/dom/vertical-headers`, docs/behaviors/vertical-headers.md; 1.9.0): the header row grows to the longest such title. Needs that feature; keys and screen readers unchanged.

columns.name: headerWrap
columns.doc: Its header's title on several lines (`@dzgrid/dom/wrapped-headers`, docs/behaviors/header-wrap.md; 1.10.0): the column headers' row grows to the tallest wrapped title, at most `maxLines`. Needs that feature.

columns.name: collapsePriority
columns.doc: With `@dzgrid/dom/responsive` (docs/behaviors/responsive-columns.md; 1.9.0): when the columns do not fit the view, which collapse under their rows first — the highest first, the last on screen among equals; 0 never. Default 1.

columns.name: filter
columns.type: false | { readonly kind?: string; readonly floating?: boolean; readonly debounceMs?: number; readonly ops?: readonly string[]; readonly optionPart?: string; readonly exclude?: false; readonly start?: 'all' | 'empty'; readonly selectAll?: boolean; readonly maxConditions?: number; readonly matchCase?: boolean; readonly condition?: boolean }
columns.doc: `false`: not filterable. `kind`: the filter kind whose UI the column shows (a built-in or a custom kind's name). `floating`: a box in the floating filter row (`@dzgrid/dom/filters`; the grid's `filters({ floating })` otherwise, `false` keeps this column out). `debounceMs`: the pause before what is typed there applies (150 in the browser, 300 on a server by default). `ops`: the operators its popup offers, in this order (the kind's own list when absent). `optionPart`: the `filterOption` part painting each row of a set filter's list (feedback pass C). `exclude: false`: its set filter never writes an `exclude` filter, nor `blanks` (docs/behaviors/filter-set.md « Include only »). `start: 'empty'`: its set list opens with nothing ticked when no filter is in force, and nothing ticked is no filter (default `'all'`); `selectAll: false`: no « Select all » box (filter-set.md « Starting empty »). Phase 9 (docs/behaviors/filter-combined.md, filter-multi.md): `maxConditions` 1 to 5, the rows its popup offers (over `filters({ maxConditions })`); `matchCase`: a « Match case » box on each text row; `condition` (a set column): a condition above the list, both stored as a `combined` AND.

columns.name: headerAlign
columns.doc: The header title's place (presentation-settings.md 3, 1.9.0): over `align`, which the title follows by default (a number column's title at the end, as its cells).

columns.name: wrap
columns.doc: The cells' text wraps on several lines (Phase 6 step 9, docs/behaviors/auto-height.md 1): with `@dzgrid/dom/auto-height` the row grows to its tallest wrapped cell; without it, or under a fixed `rowHeight`, the text wraps and is clipped.

columns.name: ui
columns.type: { readonly cell?: string; readonly header?: string; readonly tooltip?: string; readonly cellClass?: (c: CellClassContext<T, V>) => string | null | undefined; readonly headerClass?: string; readonly data?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> }
columns.doc: Parts by name for this column (a cell renderer, a header, a tooltip): plain names, resolved by the grid's registry. `cellClass` (step 26, docs/behaviors/cell-class.md): classes for a body cell from its data, space-separated (null: none). `headerClass` (showcase themes step 6): classes for the column's header cell, space-separated. `data` (feedback pass D): the app's own plain data for its parts, delivered as is (`c.column.def.ui.data`, same reference) to every part of the column. Any other key is a warning `unknown-ui-key` from the DOM layer.

columns.name: headerTooltip
columns.doc: Shown over the header, already translated by the host.

columns.name: tooltip
columns.type: (value: V | null, row: Readonly<T>, context: unknown) => string | null
columns.doc: `context`: the grid's `settings.context` (step 21).

columns.name: merge
columns.type: true | ((a: SpanCtx<T>, b: SpanCtx<T>) => boolean) | { readonly same?: (a: SpanCtx<T>, b: SpanCtx<T>) => boolean; readonly within?: readonly string[] }
columns.doc: Consecutive rows with the same value show one tall cell (docs/behaviors/spans.md). `true` compares the values' stable text; a function decides; `within` cuts a run where the listed columns change. Needs the spans feature; the base ignores it.

columns.name: rowSpan
columns.doc: How many rows this cell covers, from the data (1 when absent). Needs the spans feature.

columns.name: colSpan
columns.doc: How many columns this cell covers, from the data (1 when absent). Needs the spans feature.

columns.name: groupShow
columns.doc: Under a collapsible group (header-groups.md 1): shown only while it is open (`'open'`) or closed (`'closed'`); absent, in both. Ignored under a group that does not open and close.

columns.name: csv
columns.doc: `'text'`: in a CSV file, a digits-only value is written `="0123"` so Excel keeps it as text (csv-export.md).

columns.name: editable
columns.doc: Whether a data row's cell can be edited (editing.md 1): `true`, or a rule told the row and the grid's `settings.context`; only `true` means yes. Never a detail, filler or loading row.

columns.name: validate
columns.type: (value: V | null, row: Readonly<T>, context: unknown) => string | null | undefined
columns.doc: A refusal code (`validation.<code>` in the DOM's messages) or null: run by `@dzgrid/core/edit` after the column's `edit` checks (edit-validation.md 1). Synchronous only (owner S3-O1).

columns.name: edit
columns.doc: The simple checks of a kept value (owner S3-O3), run by `@dzgrid/core/edit`; the base reads none of it.

features.name: pagination

options.name: footer
options.doc: The footer's parts, in order (fixed): `footer.*` names, or a host's own `footer` parts.

features.doc: `pagination()`: a footer under the rows (docs/behaviors/pagination-footer.md, step 17) — what is selected, where the user is, and the pager in a named `<nav>`. Its parts `footer.selected`, `footer.count` and `footer.pager` are replaced by a host's of the same name.

features.name: quickSearch

options.name: highlight
options.doc: The words searched tinted inside the cells shown (docs/behaviors/search-highlight.md); default true.

features.doc: `quickSearch()`: the page's own search fields drive the grid's quick search (docs/behaviors/quick-search-box.md, step 16, owner decisions Q1–Q3).

features.name: csvExport

options.name: canExport
options.type: true | ((r: ExportRequest, context: unknown) => Refusal | Promise<Refusal>)
options.doc: `context`: the grid's `settings.context`, read when the export runs (step 21).

options.name: exportAll
options.doc: Server pages' `all` and `selected`: the host's export of the whole query.

options.name: fileName
options.type: (c: { readonly scope: CsvScope; readonly ctx: LocaleCtx; readonly now: number }) => string
options.doc: The file's name (`.csv` added, cleaned); default `${export.fileName}-YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm.csv` in the display zone.

options.name: onProgress
options.doc: For a host's progress bar: the grid says no progress sentences.

options.name: maxCells
options.doc: A browser export above this many cells (rows × columns) is refused; 10 000 000 by default (owner Q4).

options.name: deliver
options.type: (f: { readonly blob?: Blob; readonly url?: string; readonly fileName: string }) => void | Promise<void>
options.doc: Takes the file instead of the grid's `<a download>` (tests, a host's own saving).

options.name: loadRun
options.doc: Where the export's code comes from (`import()` of the chunk otherwise).

options.name: xlsx
options.doc: Excel files too (Phase 9): `run(scope, { format: 'xlsx' })`, `bind(button, { format: 'xlsx' })`, `xlsx.run()`. Absent: CSV only.

options.name: text
options.doc: `value` (default): machine values Excel can compute with; `display`: each cell as the grid formats it.

options.name: separator
options.doc: Default: `csvSeparatorFor(ctx)`.

options.name: bom
options.doc: A BOM first, so Excel reads UTF-8 (Arabic); default true.

options.name: header
options.doc: A line of column labels first; default true.

options.name: numbers
options.doc: `excel` (default): the locale's decimal mark unless the separator is `,`; `raw`: the machine form.

options.name: instants
options.doc: `wall` (default): the display zone's clock, seconds; `iso`: UTC with `Z`, exact.

options.name: sanitizeFormulas
options.doc: The formula guard; default true.

options.name: spans
options.doc: A spanned cell: its value in every slot it covers (`repeat`, default) or in its first only.

options.name: columns
options.doc: Column ids, in order; default the visible columns. A hidden one named is written.

options.name: tree
options.doc: A tree's depth (csv-export.md): `level` (default) a first column, 1 for the roots; `indent` two spaces per level before the tree column's text; `none` flat rows. Only when the rows are a tree's.

options.name: levelHeader
options.doc: The level column's header; default `Level`.

options.name: treeColumn
options.doc: The column that carries the indent and a filler's label; absent or not written: the first written.

options.name: groupRows
options.doc: A grouped grid's group, footer and grand total lines (Phase 7, csv-export.md « Grouped rows »): written (default), or `false` for the data rows only, flat (no level, no indent).

features.doc: `csvExport()`: the CSV export (docs/behaviors/csv-export.md, step 19) — no button of its own: the host's, bound with `bind`. This part is small; the code that builds and saves the file is a chunk loaded at the first export (or a hover). One feature object per grid.

features.name: badge

options.name: tones
options.doc: The tone of each value, by the value as a string (`String(value)`): `{ done: 'success', late: 'danger' }`.

options.name: fallback
options.doc: The tone of a value the map does not name; default `neutral`.

options.name: classes
options.doc: The host's classes per tone (showcase themes step 6), beside `dzg-badge`: `{ danger: 'bg-red-100 text-red-800' }`.

features.doc: A status badge (docs/behaviors/badge-boolean.md), registered by name and used through `ui.cell`: `parts: { statusBadge: badge({ tones: { done: 'success' } }) }`. The label is the cell's text (an enum's label; an unknown value shows the value), the tone `tones[String(value)]` (own keys only) or `fallback`; a blank shows nothing. The tone is never in the accessible name.

features.name: cellBoolean
features.doc: Yes/no cells (owner Q2), registered as `'cell.boolean'`: every boolean column takes it. True shows `✓` and `cell.yes`, false `✗` and `cell.no`, in the grid's language (the codec's `true` / `false` is not translated); a blank shows nothing. No tone: a "no" is not an error. A bundle without the texts throws here, which the grid reports.

features.name: rules
features.doc: `rules()`: selection rules (docs/behaviors/selection-rules.md, step 21). Reads `settings.selection.canSelect` and `settings.context` live: every addition is vetted through the kernel's gate, a refusal is said (a host's is told as a problem), and the boxes of rows the rule refuses now are greyed (`data-dzg-refused` on `.dzg-check`, never `aria-disabled`).

features.name: tree

options.name: column
options.doc: The column that shows the hierarchy: the first visible one by default (screen readers expect it first). A function (1.2.0) names it per data row: that row's chevron, indent and keys go there (tree-view.md « row by row »); an answer that is not a visible column's id, or a throw: the default, told once (`invalid-setting`, `tree.column`).

options.name: indent
options.doc: Pixels per level of indent (16 by default), or a data row's indent (1.2.0), for display only: an answer that is not a number from 0 to 1 000, or a throw: `level × 16`, told once (`invalid-setting`, `tree.indent`).

options.name: lazy
options.doc: Children loaded when their parent opens: `lazyChildren({ has, load })` from `@dzgrid/dom/tree-lazy` (tree-lazy.md).

options.name: sticky
options.doc: Parents kept pinned under the header while their children scroll, the nearest first (tree-sticky.md): 0 none, 3 by default.

options.name: structure
options.doc: The columns that feed the tree, read-only this phase (owner Q13, O7; the core's `edit-structure` told once for one marked editable). Default: a path tree's own column (its labels are the path), none for `parentId` or `children`; given, it replaces the default (`[]` frees a path tree's column).

options.name: parentId
options.doc: The id of a row's parent; null, undefined or '' for a root.

options.name: children
options.doc: A row's children (nested data): every level becomes rows of the grid, ids unique over all of them.

options.name: path
options.doc: A row's path of labels, root first: a level no row has becomes a filler row (a label, never data).

options.name: filter
options.doc: What a filter keeps: matches and their ancestors (default), or their whole subtrees too (tree-filter.md).

options.name: initial
options.doc: What is open at the first non-empty load: nothing (default), everything, or the levels above a depth (1: the roots).

options.name: fixedOpen
options.doc: The data rows always open (1.1.0, tree-view.md): open whatever the expansion, never closed by the kernel, never listed by expand-all / collapse-all; the DOM draws them no chevron. A throw counts as false; a value that is not a function is ignored, told (`invalid-setting`).

features.doc: `tree(options)`: the rows as a tree (docs/behaviors/tree-view.md, tree-keys.md, tree-filter.md; WAI-ARIA 1.2 treegrid). Hands `treeShape` from `@dzgrid/core/tree` to the grid's rows at creation; draws the tree column (indent, a decorative toggle), the rows' level, place and open state; opens and closes by the pointer on the toggle and by the keys of the tree column; says each opening.

features.name: lazyChildren

options.name: has
options.doc: Whether a row has children not loaded yet: read for the rows shown and a row being opened.

options.name: load
options.type: (row: T, o: { readonly signal: AbortSignalLike }) => PromiseLike<readonly T[]> | readonly T[]
options.doc: The host's loader (A): the row's children, a list or a Promise of one. A server's `children` (B) takes its place.

features.doc: `lazyChildren({ has, load })`: for `tree({ parentId, lazy })` (docs/behaviors/tree-lazy.md). A row `has` declares shows a closed toggle; opening it shows a loading row (`aria-busy`, the base's « Loading… ») while `load(row, { signal })` runs — or a server's `children` when the rows come from `sourceRows` — then its children; a failure shows the error and a Retry button (Enter on the row retries too). Nested arrays (`children`) are refused: a loaded row could not name its parent.

features.name: detail

options.name: part
options.doc: What a panel shows: a `'detail'` part (`nestedGrid(…)`, `definePart('detail', …)`), or its name in `settings.parts`.

options.name: column
options.doc: The column whose cells carry the chevron: the first visible one by default.

options.name: nested
options.doc: This grid's depth, 1 on the page; by default one more than the grids around it in the page.

options.name: height
options.doc: A detail's height: a number (default 240, owner Q4), a function of the master's row, or `'auto'` (240 until measured).

options.name: initial
options.doc: What is open at the first non-empty load: nothing (default) or every row.

options.name: isMaster
options.doc: Whether a row has a detail (master-detail.md « Rows without a detail »): asked once per row and version of the rows; a throw is no. Default: every row.

features.doc: `detail(options)`: a panel under each open master (docs/behaviors/master-detail.md, D8, owner Q4–Q5). Hands `detailShape` from `@dzgrid/core/detail` to the grid's rows at creation and places them with its sparse layout; draws a chevron in the masters' first column (forward opens, back closes); mounts the `part` in a panel at the first paint showing it (the base destroys it when its row goes); measures `'auto'` heights; names each panel « Details of » its master; says each opening by the user.

features.name: nestedGrid

options.name: settings
options.doc: The grid for a master: its rows, columns, messages, label (« Visits of … »), its own features.

options.name: keep
options.doc: How many masters' grids are remembered (sort, filters, quick search, open rows, focused cell, scroll), the least recently used forgotten first: 20.

options.name: onGrid
options.doc: Called with each grid made, once it is mounted (a host wiring its own toolbar or events).

options.name: env
options.doc: The grid's test seams (`createGrid`'s third argument): tests only.

features.doc: `nestedGrid(options)`: a ready `'detail'` part that makes a grid in each panel (master-detail.md): its own keys, scroll and focus; Enter or F2 on the panel focuses it (its focus, else the first row in view); Escape it leaves goes back to the panel's cell, one level only. Each master's sort, filters, open rows, focused cell and scroll (its top row and the offset into it) are remembered when its panel goes (closed, scrolled away) and given back when it comes again, for the last `keep` masters. A new master row or language updates the grid in place (`grid.update`); only a change of a fixed setting makes it again. Past 3 levels, the grid made tells `unsupported-combination` (`detail.depth`, owner Q5). A nested grid needs a fixed or function height (it has no natural height of its own).

features.name: edit

options.name: save
options.doc: The application's save (`@dzgrid/core/edit`, edit-save.md 1–5b); absent: a kept value is saved locally at once.

options.name: savingBorder
options.doc: The line running round a cell while it saves (Q10 amended): true by default; false, a still border.

features.doc: `edit(options)`: editing wired to the grid (Phase 5 step 4, docs/phase-5-steps/step04-plan.md): the edit controller of `@dzgrid/core/edit` on the grid's rows, what the cells show read through it, the save marks and their clocks, the rows out of the order shown, the header's reapply mark, the sentences. One feature object may serve several grids, each its own controller.

features.name: editors

options.name: enterMoves
options.doc: Q3 (revised by the owner, step 7): after Enter / Shift+Enter, the same cell (`'stay'`, default) or the cell below / above (`'down'`).

options.name: tab
options.doc: D5: Tab opens the next editable cell (`'cell'`, default) or leaves the grid (`'grid'`).

options.name: calendar
options.doc: The calendar button and Alt+Down on day and instant fields (default true); false: typing only, nothing loaded.

options.name: loadCalendar
options.doc: Where the calendar's chunk comes from (a host serving its own chunks), as `filters({ loadDates })`.

options.name: dateMessages
options.doc: tzslot's words by language, over its own EN / FR / AR (as `filters({ dateMessages })`).

options.name: list
options.doc: The list editor, `listEditor` of `@dzgrid/dom/editors-list` (owner S6-O7: its own entry). Without it a list column opens a text field read by its codec, and one warning `missing-feature` per column.

features.doc: `editors(options)`: the editors of a cell (editing.md, editors.md, edit-validation.md 3–9): text and number fields; day and instant fields with tzslot's calendar loaded on demand (`loadCalendar` replaces that import); a yes/no cell toggled in place; a list; the application's own editor (a part of slot `editor`).

features.name: listEditor
features.signature: listEditor(x: EdEnv, value: unknown, opts: readonly EnumOption[], label: (v: unknown) => string, name: string, done: (move: boolean) => void): Ed
features.doc: The list editor (editors.md 12–17, step06-plan « Behaviour » 12–17; owner S6-O2: an APG select-only combobox): the combobox in the cell keeps the focus; its listbox in a non-modal popup under the cell (above when no room), the active option by `aria-activedescendant`. Keys: Up/Down, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown (clamped); letters within 500 ms make a folded prefix, the same letter again cycles; Space picks and keeps (a letter during a prefix); a press on an option picks and keeps. A value not among the options comes first, marked. `done(move)` keeps. A blur keeps the active option: unmoved, it is the cell's own value (nothing saved, Q5). Its own entry, `@dzgrid/dom/editors-list` (owner S6-O7): an application with list columns hands it to `editors({ list: listEditor })`; one without pays nothing for it.

features.name: filters

options.name: floating
options.doc: A floating row under the headers, for every filterable column (a column's `filter.floating` wins); shown or hidden live by `floating`.

options.name: debounceMs
options.doc: The pause before a typed filter applies; 150 ms in the browser, 300 on a server by default.

options.name: popup
options.doc: The header's filter button and the popup (step 13); `false`: neither. On by default.

options.name: loadDates
options.doc: Advanced (step 14): where the date kits come from, instead of DzGrid's own `import()` of its lazy chunks (tests; a host serving its chunks its own way). A rejected promise shows the failure and Retry; a module without `adapt` is a failure.

options.name: dateMessages
options.doc: tzslot's words for a language beyond English, French and Arabic, or over them: `{ es: {...} }` (its `TzslotMessages`, in part).

options.name: dateCalendar
options.doc: The period widget's calendar: `{ months: 2 }` for two months (1 by default), `{ presets: [] }` for no shortcuts, `{ presets: ['today', 'last7Days'] }` for these, in this order (the six by default). A value it cannot take is dropped with an `invalid-setting` warning. Between two moments: no shortcuts, still.

options.name: apply
options.doc: When the popup's fields apply (owner's look, app-feedback 20): `'live'` (the default) as they change, after the pause; `'button'` only at Apply or Enter, closing without drops the draft (as on a server). The floating row and a header box stay live.

options.name: dateZone
options.doc: The instant form says its zone (`filter.zone`); `false` for an application with one zone.

options.name: busyFlash
options.doc: A brief busy state after each filter change, in milliseconds (owner's third look, app-feedback 32; off by default): `aria-busy` on the grid's root for that long, the theme's spinner over the rows (static under reduced motion). Nothing waits for it: the rows are filtered at once. For a client grid, whose filtering is instant.

options.name: loadSet
options.doc: Advanced (step 15): where the set filter's chunk comes from, instead of DzGrid's own `import()` (as `loadDates`).

options.name: maxConditions
options.doc: Phase 9 (docs/behaviors/filter-combined.md, owner Q-F2 A): the condition rows a popup offers, 1 to 5 (1 by default: today's popup); « Add condition » and one AND/OR join from 2. A column's `filter.maxConditions` wins.

options.name: matchCase
options.doc: Phase 9: a « Match case » box on each text row (off by default); a column's `filter.matchCase` wins.

options.name: rowHeight
options.doc: The floating row's height in px at 16 px text (1.10.0, filter-ui.md « Floating row height »): 24 to 1 000, grown with the text size; absent or anything else (told): the row height.

features.doc: `filters()`: the filter UI (docs/behaviors/filter-ui.md): the floating row, the popup (text, number, yes/no, the value list, tzslot's date forms loaded on demand; `loadDates` replaces that import).

features.name: range

options.name: drag
options.doc: A press and a drag of the mouse or a pen makes a block (range-selection.md 8); false: the keys, Shift+click and the API only. Default true.

options.name: canCopy
options.doc: May refuse a copy or a cut (health data): column ids and counts, never values; false or a throw refuses (clipboard.md 9).

options.name: guard
options.doc: The formula guard on copy (owner QB3); default true.

options.name: raw
options.doc: Numbers copied with a point whatever the locale (QB9); default false.

options.name: maxPaste
options.doc: Over this many cells a paste writes nothing (owner QB4); default 100 000.

options.name: clearOnOutside
options.doc: A press outside the grid clears the block, said (owner S12-Q13); not inside an element marked `data-dzg-keep-range`, nor on the page's scrollbar. false: kept (Escape clears it). Default true.

features.doc: `range(options)`: blocks of cells (docs/behaviors/range-selection.md; owner QB1, QB2, QB7, S11-Q1…Q4). Shift with the grid's own moves (mirrored right to left), Ctrl+A (every cell shown), Shift+Space (the row), the pointer (a drag, Shift+click, the auto-scroll); the tint and its logical edges on the mounted cells at each paint, aria-selected on the block's data cells only; the size said after a pause; the block dropped, said once, when the order or the rows shown change. One feature object may serve several grids, each its own block.

features.name: fill

options.name: handle
options.doc: The handle drawn, dragged and clicked (the mouse drags it; a pen only clicks it, S12-Q12); false: the keys and the API only. Default true.

options.name: along
options.doc: The one way a fill may go (1.1.0, fill.md 26): `row` along the row (toward the inline end or start), `column` up or down; every gesture's target brought back onto it. Default: both. Another value: both, an `invalid-setting` warning.

features.doc: `fill(blocks, options)`: the fill over `range()`'s block (docs/behaviors/fill.md 11–20; owner S12-Q1–Q8). The handle on the block's corner cell, or on the focused data cell (S12-Q8), re-appended at each paint; its drag (the mouse only, S12-Q12; the target outlined; the block drag's geometry and auto-scroll); a click on it then a click on a cell (WCAG 2.5.7); the keyboard mode (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter, the arrows); Ctrl/Cmd+D and Ctrl/Cmd+R; bulk edit's seam (`g.bulk`, Ctrl+Enter in the editors' field). Every way plans with `@dzgrid/core/range` (`fillTarget`, `planFill`, `planPaste`) and writes ONE commit, said once. One feature object may serve several grids.

features.name: columns

options.name: drag
options.doc: A header dragged by the mouse (never a finger, Q-M3; a pen clicks); false: the keys and the API only. Default true.

options.name: fitOnLoad
options.doc: `'content'` (1.10.0, column-resize.md 16–21): once, when the first rows are shown, the shown columns fitted to their content as « fit all » does — flexible columns, `resizable: false` ones and widths already set left alone; not again on a data change (`fitContent()` does it again).

features.doc: `columns(options)`: moving columns (docs/behaviors/column-move.md; step02-plan). A header pressed with the mouse and moved 4 px drags: a ghost of its text, a bar on the gap it lands in (logical, either direction; the segment it targets pins or unpins it), auto-scroll near the centre's edges; one `column.state` patch on release, said. Ctrl+Shift (Cmd+Shift on a Mac) + arrows, Home, End move the focused header within its segment, the place said after a pause. Registered drop targets take a drag instead (group-drop-zone.md). One feature object may serve several grids.

features.name: columnMenu

options.name: use
options.type: { readonly columns?: { api(grid: Grid): ColumnsApiLike | null }; /** With `fill`: « Fill down » / « Fill right » on the current block (owner S12-Q12). */ readonly range?: { api(grid: Grid): { get(): unknown } | null }; readonly fill?: { api(grid: Grid): { down(o?: { readonly user?: boolean }): unknown; end(o?: { readonly user?: boolean }): unknown } | null }; /** « Choose columns… » (Phase 6 step 4), opened by the column's header. */ readonly chooser?: { api(grid: Grid): { open(anchor?: HTMLElement): boolean } | null }; /** « Group by this column » / « Stop grouping by this column » (Phase 7, `grouping()`; the way without dragging, WCAG 2.5.7). */ readonly grouping?: { api(grid: Grid): { by(): readonly string[]; setBy(by: readonly string[], o?: { readonly user?: boolean }): void } | null }; /** * The pivot (`pivot()`, Phase 10, pivot.md 20): « Total » on a created column and a row total, « Mettre en colonnes » * on a data column whose header is shown. Its texts from `locales/<lang>-pivot`. */ readonly pivot?: { api(grid: Grid): { on(): boolean; by(): readonly string[]; setBy(by: readonly string[], o?: { readonly user?: boolean }): void; accepts(id: string): boolean; values(): Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; setValues(v: Readonly<Record<string, any>>, o?: { readonly user?: boolean }): void; valueColumn(id: string): string | undefined } | null } }
options.doc: The features the items drive, reached through their `api(grid)` only (typed: the menu ships none of them). Absent: their items are absent.

options.name: density
options.doc: The density line (off by default, C5; absent when `rowHeight` is a number).

options.name: onDensity
options.doc: Told after the density line changed the grid's density (owner Q3-4).

options.name: items
options.type: (column: ResolvedColumn<unknown>, defaults: readonly MenuEntry[], c: MenuContext) => readonly MenuEntry[]
options.doc: The application's items: the defaults reordered, removed or added to. A throw: the defaults, the error reported.

options.name: classes
options.type: { readonly menu?: string; readonly item?: string }
options.doc: Host classes (Tailwind, Bootstrap): on the list and on every item.

features.doc: `columnMenu(options)`: the column ⋮ menu (docs/behaviors/column-menu.md; step03-plan; owner Q-M1, Q-M2, Q-K1, Q3-1–Q3-4). A ⋮ button on each column header of 96 px and more (out of the tab order; its press never moves the focus), a right-click (Shift+right-click keeps the browser's), Shift+F10 and the Menu key, Alt+ArrowDown where the column has no filter popup, a Mac's Ctrl+click: an APG menu in the popup host — sort, pin, size, move, fill, filter, hide, choose, reset, density — each item one command (source `user`), said. Opened by a pointer, the grid's focus (and its block of cells) stays; the focus comes back where it was. One feature object may serve several grids.

features.name: contextMenu

options.name: use
options.type: { /** Copy, Copy with headers; with `edit` Cut and Paste. */ readonly range?: { api(grid: Grid): RangeApiLike | null }; /** Fill down / Fill right, by its `along`. */ readonly fill?: { api(grid: Grid): FillApiLike | null }; /** Undo / Redo; Cut and Paste need it too. */ readonly edit?: { api(grid: Grid): EditApiLike | null }; /** Export to CSV (the displayed rows). */ readonly csv?: { run(scope?: 'displayed'): Promise<unknown> }; /** Export to Excel (the displayed rows): `csvExport({ xlsx })`'s `xlsx` (Phase 9); its label `cmenu.exportXlsx` is then required. */ readonly xlsx?: { run(scope?: 'displayed'): Promise<unknown> } | undefined; /** Expand / Collapse on a parent row. */ readonly tree?: { api(grid: Grid): TreeApiLike | null }; /** Pin / Unpin the row (owner Q-CM3 A). */ readonly pinned?: { api(grid: Grid): PinnedRowsApiLike<T> | null }; /** « Read the totals » on a cell of the block (`statusBar()`, owner Q-SB3; its label from the status bar's texts). */ readonly status?: { api(grid: Grid): StatusApiLike | null } }
options.doc: The features the default items drive, through their `api(grid)` only (typed: the menu ships none of them). Absent: their items are absent.

options.name: items
options.type: (c: CellMenuContext<T>, defaults: readonly MenuEntry<CellMenuContext<T>>[]) => readonly MenuEntry<CellMenuContext<T>>[]
options.doc: The application's items: the defaults kept, reordered, removed or added to. A throw: the defaults, reported.

options.name: classes
options.type: { readonly menu?: string; readonly item?: string }
options.doc: Host classes (Tailwind, Bootstrap): on the list and on every item.

options.name: onPin
options.type: (rows: { readonly top: readonly T[]; readonly bottom: readonly T[] }) => void
options.doc: Told after « Pin » / « Unpin » changed a band (Q-CM3 A): the application keeps its pinned rows.

features.doc: `contextMenu(options)`: the cell menu (docs/behaviors/context-menu.md; context-menu-plan; owner Q-CM1–Q-CM4). A right-click on a body or band cell (Shift+right-click keeps the browser's), Shift+F10 and the Menu key on a focused cell, a Mac's Ctrl+click: the column menu's list (shared, one menu per grid) with copy, cut, paste, fill, undo, the tree's toggle, pin and export, each as its key, then the application's items. Inside the block it acts on the block; outside, the cell is focused first. Nothing to offer, a finger, a pen, an open editor: the browser's own menu.

features.name: statusBar

options.name: items
options.doc: The items, in order: `status.rows`, `status.filtered`, `status.selected`, `status.count`, `status.sum`, `status.avg`, `status.min`, `status.max`, or a host's own `status` part. Default: the block's five figures (owner Q-SB1).

options.name: maxCells
options.doc: Past this many cells a moving block shows « … » until it stops (150 ms after a key, a pointer released). Default 200 000.

features.doc: `statusBar({ items, maxCells })`: the strip under the rows (docs/behaviors/status-bar.md; owner Q-SB1–Q-SB4) — the block's count, sum, mean, smallest and largest in the column's format and the grid's digits, the row counts on request, the host's own items; one strip with the pager. Nothing is said on its own: `api(grid).announce()` and the cell menu's « Read the totals » (`contextMenu({ use: { status } })`) say it on demand.

features.name: find

options.name: debounceMs
options.doc: The pause before typed text is searched (a finite number of 0 or more); default 150 ms.

options.name: highlight
options.doc: The text tinted inside the hit cells the grid draws, the current hit's more (search-highlight.md); default true.

features.doc: `find(options)`: find in the grid (docs/behaviors/find.md; owner answers 2026-11-03). Ctrl+F (⌘F on a Mac) while the focus is in the grid opens a bar above the headers: the displayed text of the visible columns searched, case and accents ignored, rows never hidden; a closed tree node's rows too (opened to show a hit); every hit marked, the current one more, scrolled to and focused as the grid's cell; « 3 / 12 », ↑ ↓, Enter / Shift+Enter, Escape; said politely once the typing settles. A server's grid: the loaded page only, said in the bar. Without it, Ctrl+F is the browser's.

features.name: rowDrag

options.name: column
options.doc: The column whose cells show the grip (default: the first visible column); hidden, no grip.

options.name: apply
options.doc: The grid reorders its rows itself (flat browser rows only, Q-RD1); default false: the event only.

options.name: whenSorted
options.doc: Sorted or grouped rows: refused (default), or `allow`: the event is sent and the application decides (never applied).

options.name: canDrag
options.doc: A row that may not move (a throw counts as no, reported once a gesture).

options.name: canDrop
options.doc: A place a move may not go (asked at most once a frame during a drag; a throw counts as no, reported once a gesture).

options.name: maxRows
options.doc: The most rows one gesture moves (default 1 000): more is refused, said.

options.name: drag
options.doc: False: no grip, no pointer drag (the keys, the menu and the API stay). Default true.

features.doc: `rowDrag(options)`: moving rows (docs/behaviors/row-move.md; row-drag-plan.md; owner answers « Row drag », 2026-11-05). A grip at the start of a column's cells, pressed by a mouse, a pen or a finger and moved 4 px, drags the row (the selected rows when it is selected): a ghost, a line on the gap it lands in (a tree's middle: inside), auto-scroll near the top and bottom; one `rowMove` event on release. Alt+Shift+↑ / ↓ / Home / End (and → / ← in a tree) move the focused row; the cell menu's items through `menuItems`. The application reorders its rows (`moveRows`), or the grid does with `apply: true` (flat browser rows). Every way goes through `@dzgrid/core/row-drag`'s rules. One feature object may serve several grids.

features.name: dock

options.name: open
options.doc: The panels shown at the start, and where (dock.md 3): over each panel's own default. `float` is refused for now.

options.name: sizes
options.type: { readonly min?: number; readonly max?: number }
options.doc: An area's size in CSS px, between `min` (160) and `max` (800), and what leaves the rows 160 px (dock.md 9).

options.name: onChange
options.doc: After each change made by the user or the API (never a restore): the layout as a state keeps it.

features.doc: `dock(options)`: the panels beside and under the grid (docs/behaviors/dock.md; owner Q-SB5, « Dock — owner B » 2026-11-06): areas `start`, `end` and `bottom` inside the grid's box, tabs when an area holds several panels, the edge resized by the pointer and the keys (APG window splitter), collapse to a strip, « Place » to move a panel, the layout in the grid's state. The columns panel and the filters panel stand in it when both are used; an application adds its own. One feature object may serve several grids.

features.name: pivot

options.name: toggle
options.doc: A « Tableau croisé » switch for the user (pivot.md 24, 35; Q-P6 A: none by default, the mode the application's): `true` or `'inside'` in the pivot's strip above the rows (in the bar with `pivotBar()`), an element: appended into it.

options.name: valueHeaders
options.doc: The value columns' headers (pivot.md 38): `'auto'` (default) « sum(Amount) » when there are several values, the short name otherwise; `'fn'` the function form always; `'name'` the short name (`headerShort`, else `header`) only.

options.name: labelWidth
options.doc: The label column's width (default 200).

options.name: columns
options.doc: The pivot columns' ids, the first band first.

options.name: width
options.doc: A created column's width (default 120).

options.name: on
options.doc: Pivot mode (default true): off, the grouping as without the pivot.

options.name: desc
options.doc: The pivot columns whose created columns run in reverse, « (Vide) » still last (pivot.md 33).

options.name: values
options.doc: The values and their functions, in order (default: the options' `aggFuncs`, then the shown columns with an `aggFunc`).

options.name: subtotals
options.doc: A sub-total after each pivot band, per value (pivot.md 8).

options.name: maxColumns
options.doc: Above this many created columns (crossings × values, sub-totals counted), none is made (default 200; pivot.md 9).

features.doc: `pivot(options)`: a pivot table (docs/behaviors/pivot.md; Phase 10), handed to `grouping({ by, pivot: p })`. The rows are the groups, the values of the pivot columns become created columns with a total at each crossing; a label column at the start, the data columns folded away, the value columns under « Total » at the end; `spans()` draws the bands.

features.name: pivotBar

options.name: use
options.type: { /** The row grouping (`grouping({ pivot })`): the « Lignes » part. */ readonly grouping: { api(grid: Grid): { by(): readonly string[]; setBy(by: readonly string[], o?: { readonly user?: boolean }): void } | null }; /** The pivot handed to that grouping: the « Colonnes » and « Valeurs » parts. */ readonly pivot: { api(grid: Grid): PivotApi | null }; /** Moving columns (`columns()`): a header dropped on a part adds its column there. */ readonly columns?: { api(grid: Grid): { readonly dropTargets: { add(el: Element, t: { accept(column: string): boolean; drop(column: string): void; readonly label?: string }): () => void } } | null } }

options.name: panel
options.doc: The columns panel's « Mode pivot » switch and parts (pivot.md 36; default true, with `columnsChooser()`).

features.doc: `pivotBar(options)`: the pivot's one bar (docs/behaviors/pivot.md 31–37; owner 2026-11-07) — « Lignes », « Colonnes », « Valeurs », each a named `toolbar` of chips with the bands' keys (group-drop-zone.md 9, 14–18), the values' function menu, the ↑/↓ order of a pivot column, Ctrl+Shift+ArrowUp / ArrowDown (or a chip dropped there) to move a column to another part; the pivot's strip joins it; with `columnsChooser()`, the same parts and a « Mode pivot » switch at the top of the columns panel. Use it instead of the two `groupZone()` bands beside a pivot.

features.name: rowNumbers
features.doc: `rowNumbers()`: 1, 2, 3… at the inline start of every row (docs/behaviors/row-numbers.md; owner decisions 2026-11-03), in display order (a detail panel neither numbered nor counted; a paged grid going on from the pages before), as wide as its largest number. A click on a number takes the row as the block (`range()`), Shift+click the rows between; the corner every cell; without `range()`, the row selection's click; with neither, nothing. Never a column: no sort, filter, edit, export, print, copy or state sees it.

features.name: grouping

options.name: column
options.doc: The column that shows the groups' labels and chevrons: the first visible one by default (row-grouping.md 15).

options.name: indent
options.doc: Pixels per level of indent (16 by default).

options.name: sticky
options.doc: Group rows kept pinned under the header while their rows scroll, the nearest first: 0 none, 3 by default.

options.name: pivot
options.type: { make(o: GroupingOptions): GroupShape<unknown>; setup(g: GridContext<unknown>, s: GroupShape<unknown>): (FeatureHandle & { column(): string | undefined; by(): readonly string[] }) | null }
options.doc: A pivot table over the groups (`pivot()` from `@dzgrid/dom/pivot`, pivot.md 17–30); on a server only with `serverPivot()` (told).

options.name: by
options.doc: The grouping columns' ids, the first level first; empty (default): the rows flat.

options.name: aggFuncs
options.doc: Totals by column id; they win over a column's own `aggFunc`.

options.name: expanded
options.doc: What is open at the first load: nothing (default, owner Q-E1 A), everything, or the levels above a depth (1: the first).

options.name: footers
options.doc: Totals rows: none (default), a footer per open group, the grand total, or both (aggregation.md 9–10).

options.name: grandTotal
options.doc: Where the grand total sits: after the rows (default) or before them.

features.doc: `grouping(options)`: rows grouped by columns, with totals (docs/behaviors/row-grouping.md, aggregation.md; Phase 7 step 5). Hands `groupShape` from `@dzgrid/core/grouping` to the grid's rows at creation; draws the group column (indent, chevron, « value (n) »), the totals in the group and totals rows' cells, the rows' level, place and open state; opens and closes by the chevron, Enter on a group row and the keys of the group column (mirrored right to left); keeps group rows pinned under the header; says each opening. The tree's chevron styles and pinned-rows layout are shared.

features.name: groupZone

options.name: use
options.type: { /** The grouping the chips show and change. */ readonly grouping: { api(grid: Grid): GroupingApiLike | null }; /** Moving columns (`columns()`): a header dragged onto the band groups by it. Absent: no drop (the menu and the keys still work). */ readonly columns?: { api(grid: Grid): { readonly dropTargets: { add(el: Element, t: { accept(column: string): boolean; drop(column: string): void; readonly label?: string }): () => void } } | null } }

options.name: texts
options.doc: Another band's texts: `'pivot'` reads `pivot.label`, `pivot.empty`… instead of `zone.*` (the « Colonnes » band, pivot.md 19).

features.doc: `groupZone(options)`: the « Regrouper par » band (docs/behaviors/group-drop-zone.md part 2; owner Q-Z1 B, Q-Z2 A): a `toolbar` above the rows with a chip « Nom × » per grouping column, in order. A header dragged onto it (with `columns()`) groups by its column; × or Delete removes one; Ctrl+Shift+arrows or a mouse drag moves one; each change said. One tab stop, the arrows between its items (mirrored right to left).

features.name: filtersPanel

options.name: side
options.doc: The grid's side it stands on, logical: `'end'` (the default) or `'start'`; right to left puts `end` at the left.

options.name: open
options.doc: Open from the start (closed by default).

options.name: button
options.doc: The strip with the « Filters » button (on by default); `false`: the application opens it through `api(grid)`.

features.doc: `filtersPanel(options)`: every column's filter in one side panel (docs/behaviors/filters-panel.md; owner answers 2026-11-03), beside `filters()` whose forms it shows: a strip with the « Filters » button at the side the application chose, the panel beside the rows (they take the room left), « Clear all filters », a column search, each filterable column unfolding to the popup's own form, a dot on active filters; apply as `filters({ apply })`; in step with every other writer. One feature object may serve several grids.

features.name: columnsChooser

options.name: onClose
options.doc: Told after the dialog closed (the focus is already back).

features.doc: `columnsChooser(options)`: « Choisir les colonnes » (docs/behaviors/columns-chooser.md; step04-plan; owner Q-C1, Q-C2, Q-H, O1, O5, O12). A modal dialog in the popup host, anchored on the grid's root (unticking the opener's own column keeps it) and placed under the opener: a search box, every listed column in the list's order (start-pinned, centre, end-pinned, hidden ones too) inside its header groups, each a native checkbox (one tab stop, the arrows between them) with ▲ ▼ and a handle; a tick, a move, « Show all », « Reset » are each one `column.state` patch (source `user`), said; Alt+ArrowUp / ArrowDown move the focused row's column one place in the list. One feature object may serve several grids.

features.name: gridState

options.name: debounce
options.doc: The pause after a gesture before `stateChanged` (ms; 300).

options.name: persist
options.type: { readonly key: string; readonly include?: readonly StatePart[] }
options.doc: The browser storage at creation (G 17): read before the first request, written after each gesture (`include`: the parts kept).

options.name: initial
options.doc: What the grid starts with, applied before the first request (owner demo, step 16; sort.md « An initial sort »): a server is asked once, as Angular's `[state]`. Its parts only (`{ v: 1, sort: [...] }`); a stored state (`persist`) applies over it; `reset()` still goes back to the definitions.

features.doc: `gridState(o?)` (Phase 6 step 5, docs/behaviors/grid-state.md): `state()` / `setState()` on the grid, the `stateChanged` event (once per gesture, after `debounce` ms; never for the host's changes nor a restore) and `stateRestored`; with `persist`, the state kept in the browser's storage, read before the grid's first request.

features.name: pinnedRows
features.doc: `pinnedRows({ top, bottom })` (docs/behaviors/pinned-rows.md): two row groups, one sticking under the header and one at the grid's foot, named by the texts; their rows drawn like the body's (formats, parts, classes, widths, pinned columns), counted and numbered, never selected; the body's view shortened by them, both together at most half the view (a taller band shows its rows in a window moved by the wheel and the focus); the keys across the bands; their cells editable through `edit()` and `editors()` (the kernel's pinned store).

features.name: autoHeight
features.doc: `autoHeight()`: rows as tall as their tallest wrapped cell (`ColumnDef.wrap`, docs/behaviors/auto-height.md; Phase 6 step 9, owner Q-R1, Q9-1..Q9-4). After each paint, before the browser shows it (`GridContext.again`), the mounted rows not measured yet at these widths are measured — every probe written, one layout read, every probe removed — and the rows laid out again in the same frame, the row at the top of the view held where it was (S3). A fixed `rowHeight` wins (nothing measured). With `@dzgrid/dom/detail`, both layouts composed (`layoutFor`).

features.name: rowGaps

options.name: before
options.doc: Asked for each shown row but the first, once per new order of the rows shown: `true` a gap of `size`, a number that many pixels.

options.name: size
options.doc: Pixels at the default text size, scaled with the text like the row height: 16 by default.

features.doc: `rowGaps({ before, size })`: an empty space above some rows, outside every row (docs/behaviors/row-gaps.md). The core says where (`gapsOf`) and lays the rows out around the gaps (`gapLayout`); this feature asks the rule once per shown-rows version, scales the sizes with the text, hands the base its layout (`gapsFor`, always the outermost), tells the spans feature where a merge is cut (`gapAt`) and marks the row under a gap (`data-gap`, `--dzg-gap`) for a theme.

features.name: print
features.signature: print(grid: PrintableGrid, o?: PrintOptions | undefined): Promise<void>

options.name: maxRows
options.doc: Rows printed at most (5 000 by default, owner Q-I); beyond, the first ones, a line saying so, and `print-too-many`.

options.name: title
options.doc: The table's caption; the grid's accessible name otherwise.

options.name: header
options.doc: `false`: no header rows (hidden-headers.md 6); printed by default, a grid with `headers: 'hidden'` too.

features.doc: `print(grid, options)`: `preparePrint`, the browser's print dialog, and the cleanup on `afterprint` — or on the first `focus` or `pointerdown` after the dialog, for a browser that sends no `afterprint` (Safari's PDF path; the cleanup is idempotent, so the later ones do nothing). A build cancelled or overtaken by a newer call opens no dialog: only the newest prints, and each cleanup removes its own table only.

features.name: printOnMenu
features.signature: printOnMenu(grid: PrintableGrid, o?: PrintOptions | undefined): void

options.name: maxRows
options.doc: Rows printed at most (5 000 by default, owner Q-I); beyond, the first ones, a line saying so, and `print-too-many`.

options.name: title
options.doc: The table's caption; the grid's accessible name otherwise.

options.name: header
options.doc: `false`: no header rows (hidden-headers.md 6); printed by default, a grid with `headers: 'hidden'` too.

features.doc: `printOnMenu(grid, options)`: from then on, `beforeprint` builds the print table at once (a table built in slices would be cut at its first slice), unless one is already in the page (`print()`'s, or one the application prepared: that one prints); it is removed as `print()` removes its own (`afterprint`, else the first `focus` or `pointerdown`). It lasts as long as the grid: its destruction ends it.

features.name: freshRows

options.name: ms
options.doc: How long a new row stays marked, in ms: 5000 by default, from 0 to 60 000.

options.name: rowsArrived
options.doc: Told once per refresh, with the keys of the rows marked (never row data) and who changed the rows; a throw is reported.

features.doc: `freshRows({ ms })` (docs/behaviors/fresh-rows.md, owner Q16-9 A): the rows a live change of the rows added (a delta: a transaction, or a reload or a server's answer for the same page and query compared by `sameRow`) and the query keeps get `data-dzg-fresh` for `ms` wherever they are drawn; one polite sentence counts them; `rowsArrived` is given their keys. Never on a first load, a page, a sort or a filter (new answers, not arrivals). Its look: `@dzgrid/theme/fresh-rows.css`.

features.name: motion

options.name: preset
options.doc: How it feels; `sober` (the only one yet): short, eased, no bounce.

options.name: gsap
options.doc: The application's GSAP; else the chunk imports the package itself.

options.name: onCell
options.type: (el: HTMLElement, c: CellMotion, reason: 'changed' | 'saving' | 'saved' | 'failed') => void | false
options.doc: A cell whose value a transaction changed (`changed`), or whose save started (`saving`, once per gesture), succeeded (`saved`) or was refused (`failed`), with `@dzgrid/dom/edit` (Phase 5 step 7); after the grid's guards (at most 50 cells, and 50 calls a paint for all reasons; under reduced motion too, `c.reduced` true). Animate `el` only (transform, opacity, `--dzg-*`, classes). `false`: handled, the built-in flash (`changed`, `saved`) is skipped. Either way `el` is followed: its tweens are finished when it shows another row or its next reason.

options.name: onRow
options.type: (el: HTMLElement, c: RowMotion, reason: 'entered' | 'moved') => void | false
options.doc: A row that moved or entered after a sort, a filter or a tree's toggle, or that was added live (owner Q5; not under reduced motion).

features.doc: `motion()`: rows gliding after a sort or a filter, a value flash on live changes, a page slide, popups and the overlay fading in (docs/behaviors/motion.md, step 26). This part is small; the tweens and GSAP are a chunk loaded in idle time once the first rows are painted (owner Q1). One `motion()` may serve several grids.

features.name: totalsRow
features.doc: `totalsRow()` (docs/behaviors/totals-row.md): the columns' `total` (`sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`, `first`, `last` or a function; the group totals' rules, `@dzgrid/core/totals`) over the rows that pass the filters, through the edits, in one row last in the pinned bottom band — no data, read-only, never selected — its label (`totals.label`) in the first column without a total. Computed again only when the rows, the edits, the columns or the language changed. CSV, Excel and print write it; JSON does not. With a server's pages, the application gives the totals (`api.set`).

features.name: verticalHeaders

options.name: maxHeight
options.doc: The header row's height at most, in px (240 by default); a longer title is cut with « … ».

features.doc: `verticalHeaders()` (docs/behaviors/vertical-headers.md): the headers of the columns marked `headerVertical: true` say `data-vertical` (the theme turns their title a quarter counter-clockwise), and the column headers' row grows to the longest such title — measured on a hidden probe, once per change of the titles, the row height or the density, never at a scroll — at least a row's height, at most `maxHeight`. Names, roles and keys unchanged.

features.name: theming
features.doc: `theming()` (docs/behaviors/presentation-settings.md 16–23, 1.9.0): writes `settings.theme` as CSS variables on the grid's root and draws `settings.icons` over the grid's marks, both live; a bad key, value or icon is told (`invalid-setting`) and skipped, never thrown. Its own entry, so a grid without them carries none of it.

options.name: maxLines
options.doc: The lines a title may take, 1 to 10 (3 by default); past them its last line ends with « … ».

features.name: columnHover
features.doc: `columnHover()` (docs/behaviors/column-hover.md, 1.10.0): the column under the mouse or the pen — never the keyboard's focus, never a finger — says `data-hover-col` on the grid's root and `data-col-hover` on its mounted cells and header, written at most once per frame and only when the column changes; attributes only, no layout or style read.

features.name: responsive

options.name: priority
options.doc: A collapse priority by column id, over the columns' own `collapsePriority`: the highest collapse first; 0 never.

features.doc: `responsive({ priority })` (docs/behaviors/responsive-columns.md): when the columns do not fit the view, centre columns collapse — the highest `collapsePriority` first, the last on screen among equals, never the first, a pinned one or a priority 0 — and each row's chevron (the detail's) opens « Title: value » lines under it. Followed at each paint; not the columns' state; the search, filters, files and print still read every column.

features.name: fileImport

options.name: accept
options.doc: The formats taken (both by default); another is refused, `import-file` detail `type`.

options.name: onRows
options.type: (rows: Record<string, unknown>[], problems: readonly Problem[], file: ImportedFile) => void
options.doc: The rows read, once per file: one object per line after the header, each value at its column's `field` (or id) as its codec reads it; `problems` what was refused (paths and codes, never a value). The application decides what to do.

options.name: drop
options.doc: `false`: no drop zone (the button only).

features.doc: `fileImport({ accept, onRows, drop })` (docs/behaviors/file-import.md): a CSV or `.xlsx` file dropped on the grid, or picked through the application's button (`api(grid).bind(button)`), read in the browser — the first non-empty line the header matched to the columns, each cell through its column's codec — and handed to `onRows`; the grid's rows untouched. Said when read.

features.name: spans
features.signature: spans(o?: { readonly acrossLevels?: boolean; } | undefined): GridFeature

options.name: acrossLevels
options.doc: In a tree (1.2.0, opt-in, spans.md « Across levels »): outside a row's tree column, a merge continues across a node and its children shown, under one top-level row. Without it a merge stops at a level change (1.1.0).

features.doc: `spans()`: cells spanning rows and columns (docs/behaviors/spans.md) — identical values merged (`merge`), spans decided by the data (`rowSpan`, `colSpan`), full-width rows (`settings.fullWidth`), grouped headers (groups in `columns`, `./bands.ts`). The map comes from the core (`buildSpanMap`), on the rows as displayed and the visible columns; this feature lays it out under virtual scrolling, moves the keys over it and maps a click on a tall cell to the row under the pointer.

features.name: groups
features.doc: `groups()`: collapsible header groups (Phase 6 step 7, docs/behaviors/header-groups.md; owner Q-GH, Q8-4), with `spans()` (the group rows). Its own entry, loaded only with collapsible groups.

features.name: slots
features.doc: `slots()`: a host's parts draw the column headers' labels, the overlay, the busy mark (1.4.0) and the tooltip in place of the grid's own (docs/behaviors/parts.md, step 11). The grid keeps the rest: the header's role, sort state, mark, grip and click; the overlay's place and retry button; the tooltip's element, timing, Escape and placement.
